data.message:
fix(call): deliver call signals over Gun; no WSS broadcast for calls

Final-review fixes:
- Gun inbox emit dropped callId/meta, so every invite was discarded (C1).
- Call kinds skip the relay's generic WSS broadcast, which either rejects
  rtc-call-* or fans SDP/ICE (IPs) out to all clients (C2). Gun only.
- Known-contact gate waits for signaling init before reading the chat cache (I1).
- Post-await failures ignored once the pc/call is stale (I2); glare loser
  resets mute/camera/remote stream (M1).

data.message:
feat: replace BlockCypher with multi-provider Bitcoin API fallback

Remove unreliable BlockCypher API (returns 404 on valid confirmed txs).
Add three free providers tried in order:
- mempool.space (primary)
- blockstream.info (fallback)
- blockchain.info (tertiary, 2-step block hash lookup)

All providers normalize to {blockHash, opReturnHex} contract.
Configurable via BITCOIN_API_ORDER env var.
Add parseOpReturnHex() for scriptpubkey format parsing.
Update .env-sample and Serena project memories accordingly.
All 70 tests pass.

data.message: Isolate approval verifier while preserving the frozen baseline

registry: crc.nodes.v0 — nodes.json format fixed (Pavlo's lane precondition)

Fixed field set, null-not-absent, append-only (retirement = tombstone,
never deletion). Registering = one PR adding one node object; merges on
parse + conformance + checkable key_ref, no other approval step.

Cell delivery contract: in-repo cells/{claim_id}/{node_id}.cell.json
(default, CI-validated) or self-hosted cell_url_template; unreachable =
pending-abstain. Failed envelope checks land in cells/rejected/ with the
error — non-suppression, same as claims.

claim_sources: ledger-only per the 2026-08-05 group decision.
Seeded with node 1 (invinoveritas, nostr-nip01) + node 2 (Vertice
recompute-lens, eip712) exactly as their #236 v1 Cells identify.

data.message:
ci: publish to npm on tag, with guards that make "green" mean published (#11)

npm sat on 0.7.0 for three months while main was on 0.8.0, because publishing was
manual and nothing failed when nobody ran it. That gap was not cosmetic: 0.7.0
predates the 8309 divergence-preservation work, so `npm i ccip-router` shipped a node
that keys retention by inputHash, reads multi-vantage attestations as equivocation,
drops them, and flags the honest peer for slashing.

Three guards, which are the point of the job rather than the publish:

- the tag must equal package.json's version, so v0.9.0 cannot publish 0.8.0 silently
- an already-published version is skipped, so re-running a failed job is safe instead
  of failing on a 403 that reads like a credentials problem
- after publishing, wait for the registry to actually serve the version. npm prints
  "+ ccip-router@x.y.z" and separately warns it "may take a few minutes to become
  available" — those are different claims, and going green on the first reports a
  publish that may not have landed

Publishes with --provenance so the tarball is traceable to the commit and run.

NPM_TOKEN must be a granular token with "Bypass 2FA" enabled; a classic automation
token authenticates and then fails the publish with a 403 that looks like a
permissions problem and is not one.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

data.message:
run_conformance: reject number tokens the parser would round (1e999/2e999 -> inf, 1e-999 -> 0, digits past a double)

Strict JSON rejected the NaN/Infinity constants but not legal numeric tokens
that overflow, underflow or lose precision when parsed, so two different
evidence values could compare equal after parsing. Accept a number token only
when its decimal value is exactly the double it parses to (or that double's
shortest repr). Applies to both the corpus and the report.

Control: test_distinct_number_tokens_never_collapse_to_one_value (8 subtests
fail on the previous head, all pass here), with positive controls for ordinary
spellings of exact doubles.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
